ra: The Hak-Muhammad-Ali triad is the divine center invoked at the Kirklar assembly / cem; grouped under the cohort hub as core Alevi cosmology.
Haji Bektash is the eponymous pir of the tradition centered on the Kirklar/cem archetype; wired to the cohort hub.
Pir Sultan Abdal is a saint of the same Alevi tradition whose hymns are sung in the cem rooted in the Kirklar archetype.
The cem is the living enactment of the Kirklar assembly; grouped under the hub.
Hizir is a venerated holy figure of the Alevi tradition organized around the Kirklar/cem; wired to the hub.
The Twelve Imams are venerated throughout Alevi devotion centered on the cem/Kirklar; grouped under the hub.
The Kizilbash are the historical Alevi community whose tradition centers on the Kirklar/cem archetype; wired to the hub.
The Abdalan-i Rum are the dervish milieu of the Alevi-Bektashi tradition organized around the cem/Kirklar; grouped under the hub.
The semah turning dance is performed within the cem ceremony.
The dede leads and presides over the cem gathering.
Dedes derive their authority from descent within a sacred ocak lineage.
The cem is explicitly understood as the re-enactment of the primordial assembly of the Forty.
The Muharrem/matem mourning fast commemorates Husayn and the Twelve Imams.
The Buyruk is the doctrinal corpus of the Alevi tradition centered on the cem/Kirklar; grouped under the hub.
Balim Sultan, the pir-i sani, organized Bektashi ritual life around the cem/Kirklar archetype; wired to the hub.
Kaygusuz Abdal is a foundational Bektashi saint-poet of the tradition centered on the cem/Kirklar.
In Alevi-Bektashi lore the assembly of the Forty is presided over by Ali (existing ENT_ISL_ALI), the central holy figure of the tradition.
The Alevi Hak-Muhammad-Ali triad receives Ali ibn Abi Talib (existing) as the locus of divine manifestation.
The Alevi triad incorporates the Prophet Muhammad (existing ENT_ISL_MUHAMMAD).
The triad's Hak (the Truth/God) is the Alevi reception of Allah (existing ENT_ISL_ALLAH).
ENT_ALV_HAJI_BEKTASH is the Alevi-Bektashi veneration of the historical Hajji Bektash Wali recorded at existing ENT_SUF_BEKTASH (homonymous figure, two tradition-receptions).
Haji Bektash is the eponym and pir of the Bektashiyya order (existing ENT_SUF_BEKTASHI), the institutional wing of the Alevi-Bektashi tradition.
Alevi Hizir is the reception of the immortal Khidr (existing ENT_ISL_KHIDR); homonymous figure across traditions.
The Alevi On Iki Imam are the reception of the Twelve Imams found within the Shi'a Fourteen Infallibles (existing ENT_ISL_INFALLIBLES).
Alevi veneration of the Imams continues devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt (existing ENT_ISL_AHL_BAYT).
The twelfth of the venerated Imams is the hidden Mahdi (existing ENT_ISL_MAHDI), awaited in Alevi eschatology.
The Muharrem/matem mourning commemorates the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali (existing ENT_ISL_HUSAYN) at Karbala.
Ocak lineages claim genealogical descent from the Ahl al-Bayt (existing ENT_ISL_AHL_BAYT), grounding dede authority.
Pir Sultan Abdal stands in the Anatolian Turkish saint-poet (asik) tradition exemplified by Yunus Emre (existing ENT_SUF_YUNUS_EMRE); functional/literary alignment, not identity.
The Alevi divinization-of-Ali motif draws on the antinomian Sufi current of divine immanence exemplified by al-Hallaj's 'Ana al-Haqq' (existing ENT_SUF_HALLAJ); doctrinal alignment of theme.
The Buyruk corpus is traditionally ascribed in part to Ja'far al-Sadiq (existing ENT_ISL_SADIQ); attested ascription, not historical authorship.
